Poplar sits south of Highway 1, around Huntingdon Road, King Road and Gladwin Road.
The board name is Poplar, while the City's official demographic profile name for the same area is South Poplar, profile area 5.
The area runs west of the Marshall Road and McCallum Road side and east toward Clearbrook Road.
Clearbrook lies to the northwest, the City Centre and South Fraser Way corridor lie north across Highway 1, and Sumas Prairie lies to the east and southeast.
No Poplar-specific neighbourhood plan is listed in the Official Community Plan; Abbotsforward 2050 governs.
The community was named Poplar for the poplar trees planted on the top of the hill, and the Old South Poplar School is on the Abbotsford Community Heritage Register.
Single detached houses are the main form, on urban lots in the north part and larger rural lots toward Huntingdon Road and the south edge.
Urban minimums are RS3 at 540 m² and RS5 at 420 m² minimum interior lots in City reports, while rural A1 land subdivides at a minimum of 8.0 ha.
The established stock is freehold detached housing, with strata limited to the townhome complexes noted above.

Lots inside the Airport Zoning Regulation area on City drawing M-500 face height surfaces and NAV CANADA and Transport Canada approvals before a City permit, because Poplar is east of Abbotsford International Airport (YXX).
Floodplain status for a single lot is checked against Zoning Bylaw Schedule E Floodplain Boundaries in the City WebMap.

blocks.text: Poplar: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Both locator-run addresses in Poplar return the same regular chain: Jackson Elementary, Abbotsford Middle and Abbotsford Senior Secondary, including Jackson Elementary's own address at 33165 King Road.
Huntingdon Park is at 34779 3rd Avenue and Berry Park at 33928 Fern Street at the north edge toward Highway 1.
The nearest City recreation centres are outside the area: Matsqui Recreation Centre at 3106 Clearbrook Road to the northwest and Abbotsford Recreation Centre at 2499 McMillan Road to the northeast.
Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre at 32900 Marshall Road sits immediately north and northeast of Poplar across Highway 1.
South-edge rural lots may be on wells and onsite sewage, recorded in the provincial GWELLS database and under the Sewerage System Regulation through Fraser Health.

A district-wide school renaming note for nearby Matsqui-area buyers: the former Matsqui Elementary is now Mathxwí Elementary at 33661 Elizabeth Avenue, renamed at the end of 2021 in consultation with local First Nation communities.
Kings Crossing, 1641 King Crescent: 20 townhomes by Rockwood Homes Inc., selling with completion expected in 2026 per the developer page. Status (as of November 3, 2026): selling.

King and McKenzie Roads sports park proposal: the City conditionally acquired a King Road property for a future sports and recreation park, subject to Agricultural Land Commission approval, offering about 50 acres along LeFeuvre Road for inclusion in the ALR. Status (as of November 3, 2026): the Commission denied the exclusion application on August 20, 2026, and Council directed staff on August 25, 2026 to review options.

The Poplar point is the tax formula itself: Abbotsford tax is the BC Assessment value multiplied by a rate per $1,000 of net assessed value, and about 35 cents of each tax dollar passes to other taxing authorities.
Highway 1 runs along the north edge with interchanges at McCallum Road and Clearbrook Road.
Huntingdon Road leads toward the Huntingdon/Sumas border crossing via Highway 11 and Sumas Way, and Highway 11 to the east connects Abbotsford to Mission.
Gladwin Road and Marshall Road run north–south, and King Road and Huntingdon Road run east–west.
Exchanges serving the area are Clearbrook Centre and Bourquin Exchange.
Check floodplain status lot by lot against Zoning Bylaw Schedule E in WebMap, because drainage runs toward the Sumas Prairie system.
Confirm ALR status before counting on subdivision or an extra dwelling on a south-edge lot, where the A1 minimum is 8.0 ha.
Check AZR status on City drawing M-500 before planning additions on lots east of YXX.
On rural lots, pull the GWELLS well record and confirm septic filings before removing subjects.

blocks.text: South of Highway 1, Poplar splits in two. The north end has suburban streets around Marshall Road; toward the border, along King Road and Huntingdon Road, it opens up into acreages.

faq.a: Three public schools sit inside the area. South Poplar Traditional Elementary is at 32746 Huntingdon Road, Jackson Elementary at 33165 King Road and Abbotsford Traditional School at 2272 Windsor Street, and the catchment for any single address must still be checked in the locator.
faq.q: Which schools are physically in Poplar?

faq.a: Abbotsford Traditional School runs Grades 6 to 12 and feeds from two elementary schools. The school states the majority of its Grade 6 students come from King and South Poplar, and feeder students are automatically registered.
faq.q: How does the Traditional pathway work here?

faq.a: Four routes serve the area. Route 3 runs Clearbrook/Huntingdon, route 5 runs Clearbrook/Bourquin via Hospital on Marshall Road at the east edge, route 6 runs the Gladwin corridor and route 12 links the University of the Fraser Valley and Bourquin Exchange.
Poplar drains toward the Sumas Prairie system the City describes as low-lying and subject to Nooksack River overflow, so the Schedule E map in WebMap must be checked for the specific lot.

Yes — Abbotsford Traditional School states the majority of its Grade 6 students come from its two feeder elementary schools, King and South Poplar, and feeder-school students are automatically registered there for Grades 6–12; the Traditional program is a choice program, so this is a feeder/entry fact, not a catchment assignment.
faq.q: Is South Poplar a feeder school for Abbotsford Traditional?

faq.a: BC Transit route 3 runs Clearbrook / Huntingdon, route 5 runs Clearbrook / Bourquin via Hospital on Marshall Road at the east edge, route 6 runs the Gladwin corridor and route 12 links UFV and Bourquin Exchange via Jackson Street and McCallum Park and Ride.
